== Biography ==
William Glasgow was recorded as the 40-year-old head of house 1 at Cloughgaldenagh, Dunaghy, County Antrim, in the surviving 1851 census. He was a weaver, could read and write, and was living with his wife [[Unknown-540868|Ellin Glasgow]], also aged 40 and a weaver. The return records County Antrim as their birthplace and 1831 as the year of their first marriage.<ref name="Census1851">“1851 Irish Census Returns,” Cloughgaldenagh house 1, Dunaghy, County Antrim, detailed public transcription, [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf PDF]; see also [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Killcondray/Dunaghy/Galdernaugh/1/ National Archives of Ireland household page] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QV9Y-WFJ7 FamilySearch QV9Y-WFJ7].</ref>

The household contained eight children, all recorded as born in County Antrim:<ref name="Census1851"/>

The census does not name William's father. His attachment to [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]] is therefore retained as uncertain and should not be treated as proved by the 1851 household.

The later Griffith's Valuation index for Dunaghy does not list William at Cloughgaldenagh.<ref>“Griffith's Valuation, North Mid Antrim,” Dunaghy index, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1860griffiths/northmidantrimgriffiths.pdf PDF].</ref> This negative finding does not establish his death, migration, or loss of tenancy.
* Death index entry: William Glasgow, 14 September 1874, aged 58, Belfast district, D/1874/49/1007/17/123. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].

== Research Notes ==
=== Late William Alexander Glasgow, named in 1875 ===

Emma’s marriage notice names her father as the late William Alexander Glasgow. She married William, second son of Robert Treacy, on 4 September 1875 at St Thomas’s Church, Belfast. Both spouses were of Parsonstown; that wording does not state her late father’s own residence, birthplace or place of death. His age, occupation, wife and parents are unstated.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1265675182/ Belfast Evening Telegraph, 4 September 1875, p.2].</ref>

An ordinary William with no recorded middle name remains compatible. The Belfast death in 1874 and a possible later daughter fit this family comparison; the 1851 household’s absence of Emma does not exclude a child born later. The source does not identify this William as William Alexander. [[Glasgow-1737|William Glasgow of Killycurragh]], [[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow who died in Ohio in 1855]], and [[Glasgow-3952|William Glasgow associated with County Limerick]] remain lower comparisons. The c.1815 [[Glasgow-2771|Emma Glasgow]] hypothesis cannot be combined with this William’s c.1810 birth.
